explanations: Cyan is the colour between blue and green on the spectrum, and is what is left when red is taken out of white.
Magenta is a purplish pink, midway between blue and red, and started life in 1859 as the aniline dye fuchsine.
Yellow lies between green and orange; carotenoids give it to autumn leaves and daffodils, and a screen makes it from red and green.
Cyan, magenta and yellow are the subtractive inks of colour printing; a fourth, black, is added as the key plate, giving CMYK.

sources.excerpt: Cyan () is the color between blue and green on the visible spectrum of light.
Cyan is the complement of red; it can be made by the removal of red from white.
Magenta is a purplish-pink color. On color wheels of the RGB and CMYK color models, it is located directly midway between blue and red.
Magenta took its name from an aniline dye made and patented in 1859 by the French chemist François-Emmanuel Verguin [fr], who originally called it fuchsine.
Carotenoids give the characteristic yellow color to autumn leaves, corn, canaries, daffodils, and lemons, as well as egg yolks, buttercups, and bananas.
In the RGB color model, used to create colors on television and computer screens, yellow is a secondary color made by combining red and green at equal intensity.
The abbreviation CMYK refers to the four color components used in printing: cyan, magenta, yellow, and black (the key plate).
